bib.title: DeepSeek-V2: A Strong, Economical, and Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Language Model

read.skipped: Appendix G evaluation-format example tables 12-37 (benchmark prompt examples) and the reference list past a skim; not needed for method or results.

question: Can an MoE language model with a compressed-KV attention (MLA) and DeepSeekMoE give top-tier open-source quality with cheaper training and much cheaper inference than a dense model?
hypothesis: Low-rank joint key-value compression (MLA) can cut the KV cache heavily while matching or beating MHA quality, unlike GQA and MQA, which trade quality for cache size.
contributions: MLA: low-rank joint KV compression with decoupled RoPE, caching (d_c + d_h^R) elements per token per layer
DeepSeekMoE with device-limited routing, three auxiliary balance losses and device-level token dropping
236B-total / 21B-active model pretrained on 8.1T tokens, extended to 128K context with YaRN, then SFT and GRPO RL

method.summary: A 60-layer Transformer whose attention is MLA (KV latent of 512 plus a 64-dim decoupled RoPE key) and whose FFNs, except layer 1, are DeepSeekMoE (2 shared + 160 routed experts, 6 active). Pretrained on 8.1T tokens at 4K sequence length, extended to 128K with YaRN, then SFT (1.5M instances) and two-stage GRPO RL.
method.task: next-token pretraining of an MoE LM, then SFT and RL alignment; efficiency comparison against dense DeepSeek 67B

datasets.name: DeepSeek-V2 pretraining corpus
datasets.size: 8.1T tokens (Chinese tokens about 12% more than English)
datasets.source: multi-source; more Chinese data than the DeepSeek 67B corpus; contentious content filtered
datasets.preprocessing: same stages as DeepSeek 67B with improved cleaning and quality filtering; BBPE tokenizer

datasets.name: SFT data
datasets.source: internal, covers math, code, writing, reasoning, safety

datasets.name: RL preference data
datasets.source: code preference from compiler feedback; math preference from ground-truth labels
datasets.preprocessing: quality filtering and proportion adjustment (no sizes given)

datasets.name: Benchmarks (MMLU, C-Eval, CMMLU, HellaSwag, PIQA, ARC, BBH, TriviaQA, NQ, RACE, DROP, C3, CMRC, WinoGrande, CLUEWSC, Pile-test, CHID, CCPM, GSM8K, MATH, CMath, HumanEval, MBPP, CRUXEval, AGIEval, IFEval, LiveCodeBench, MT-Bench, AlpacaEval 2.0, AlignBench)
datasets.source: public; LiveCodeBench questions 1 Sep 2023 to 1 Apr 2024

other.MoE: all FFNs except first layer; 2 shared + 160 routed experts, expert intermediate dim 1536, 6 routed active
other.KV cache per token: (d_c + d_h^R) l elements = 576 per layer, equal to GQA with 2.25 groups (d_c=4 d_h, d_h^R=d_h/2)
other.extra: RMS Norm after compressed latents and scaling factors at width bottlenecks

models.name: DeepSeek 67B
models.architecture: dense MHA-family (GQA per prior release; not stated here)

training.objective: next-token prediction (pretraining); SFT; GRPO RL with group-relative advantage and KL penalty
training.lr_schedule: warmup-and-step-decay: x0.316 after about 60% of tokens, again x0.316 after about 90%
training.warmup: linear from 0 to max over first 2K steps
training.batch_size: scheduled from 2304 to 9216 over the first 225B tokens, then 9216
training.regularisation: gradient clipping norm 1.0; balance losses alpha1=0.003 (expert), alpha2=0.05 (device), alpha3=0.02 (communication); device-limited routing M=3, D=8; token dropping with capacity factor 1.0 and about 10% of sequences never dropped (training only)
training.hardware: NVIDIA H800 cluster, 8 GPUs/node on NVLink and NVSwitch, InfiniBand across nodes
training.compute: 172.8K H800 GPU hours per trillion tokens (DeepSeek 67B: 300.6K)

other.parallelism: 16-way zero-bubble pipeline, 8-way expert parallel, ZeRO-1 data parallel, no tensor parallel
other.framework: HAI-LLM with custom CUDA kernels; MLA kernel based on an improved FlashAttention-2
other.YaRN: scale s=40, alpha=1, beta=32, target max context 160K, length factor sqrt(t)=0.0707 ln s + 1, applied to the decoupled key
other.RL: two stages (reasoning alignment with RM_reasoning, then multi-reward preference alignment); reward models initialised from DeepSeek-V2 Chat (SFT); RL inference backend vLLM; epsilon, beta, group size G, RL lr and steps not given
other.V2-Lite training: lr 4.2e-4, x0.316 at 80% and 90% of tokens, constant batch 4608, alpha1=0.001, 5.7T tokens

inference.prompting: few-shot counts per benchmark in Table 2 and 3; perplexity-based eval for multiple-choice sets, generation-based for the rest; no token dropping at evaluation

other.deployment: parameters converted to FP8; KV cache quantised to 6 bits per element on average
other.throughput test: prompt and generation length distribution from the deployed DeepSeek 67B service, single node of 8 H800

results.claim: DeepSeek-V2 cuts the KV cache by 93.3% against dense DeepSeek 67B.
results.setup: DeepSeek-V2 (MLA, MoE, KV cache quantised to 6 bits on average) vs DeepSeek 67B; the figure bundles MLA, quantisation and architecture differences
results.note: Not isolated to MLA; paper does not report an MLA-only figure at full scale.

results.claim: Maximum generation throughput is 5.76 times that of DeepSeek 67B.
results.setup: Single node of 8 H800 GPUs, FP8 weights, 6-bit KV cache, prompt/generation length distribution from the deployed 67B service
results.quote: which is 5.76 times the maximum generation throughput of DeepSeek 67B

results.claim: Generation throughput exceeds 50K tokens per second on one 8-GPU H800 node.
results.quote: DeepSeek-V2 achieves a generation throughput exceeding 50K tokens per second

results.claim: Prompt input throughput exceeds 100K tokens per second.
results.quote: the prompt input throughput of DeepSeek-V2 exceeds 100K tokens per second

results.claim: Training costs 42.5% less than dense DeepSeek 67B (172.8K vs 300.6K H800 GPU hours per trillion tokens).
results.setup: Practical training on the H800 cluster, per trillion tokens
results.quote: DeepSeek 67B requires 300.6K GPU hours, while DeepSeek-V2 needs only 172.8K GPU hours

results.claim: MLA caches (d_c + d_h^R) l elements per token, about 9/2 d_h l, equal to GQA with 2.25 groups.
results.setup: DeepSeek-V2 with d_c=4 d_h=512 and d_h^R=64 (d_h=128); elements, not bytes
results.quote: MLA requires only a small amount of KV cache, equal to GQA with only 2.25 groups, but can achieve stronger performance than MHA.

results.claim: In MoE ablations MLA used 14% (small) and 4% (large) of the MHA KV cache.
results.setup: Small MoE ~16B total on 1.33T tokens; large MoE ~250B total on 420B tokens; same architecture except attention. Cache 15.6K vs 110.6K and 34.6K vs 860.2K elements/token
results.quote: MLA requires a significantly smaller amount of KV cache (14% for small MoE models and 4% for large MoE models) than MHA.

YaRN plus 1000 steps at 32K extend the context from 4K to 128K with good NIAH results.

results.claim: Decoupled RoPE is needed because RoPE blocks absorbing W^UK into W^Q, which would force recomputing prefix keys.
results.setup: Argument in Sec 2.1.3, no ablation of this choice
results.quote: we must recompute the keys for all the prefix tokens during inference, which will significantly hinder the inference efficiency.

results.claim: Fewer than 10K SFT instances caused a significant IFEval decline.
results.quote: we observe a significant performance decline on the IFEval benchmark if we use fewer than 10K instances

limits: The 93.3% / 5.76x headline figures compare against dense DeepSeek 67B and bundle MLA, MoE sparsity, FP8 weights and 6-bit KV quantisation; no MLA-only efficiency ablation at full scale is given.
MLA vs MHA quality ablation is on two scales with different token budgets (1.33T and 420B) and activated parameters differ between arms; single runs, no seeds.

Throughput test uses the prompt/length distribution of the DeepSeek 67B service; batch size, hardware utilisation and kernel details are not given, and no prefill vs decode breakdown beyond one prompt-throughput number.
RL hyperparameters (epsilon, beta, G, lr, steps) and RL data sizes are not stated; no seeds.
Authors concede: no knowledge updates after pretraining, possible hallucination, limited proficiency outside Chinese and English, text only; alignment tax on BBH.
